summary: Sketch relations now show on the canvas as small marks in the dimension colour, drawn as the same symbol that the Constrain menu and the relations list now show beside each relation. Horizontal or Vertical between a line's own ends sits beside the middle of that line, toward the inside of the sketch, and between points of different edges marks each point; Parallel, Perpendicular, Collinear and Equal length mark each line; Equal radius marks the arc or circle, at the top of a circle or the middle of an arc, and Point on curve marks its point and the arc or circle; Coincident, Midpoint, Point on line and a fixed point mark their point; Symmetric marks both points and the axis; Tangent marks the joint. A point that Fix holds shows the Fixed mark. A point kept On the X axis or On the Y axis shows the Coincident mark, after the Constrain tool that puts it there, and a point kept on both shows one Coincident mark named At the origin while the relations list keeps both rows. A coordinate held away from 0, or one that follows a parameter, is a Distance dimension since 0.0.782 and draws as one with no mark, so a point with one coordinate on an axis and the other away from it shows the on-axis mark and the Distance. A Coincident relation between two arc or circle centers reads Concentric on the canvas, in the relations list, in constraint issues and in the status line. Points that Coincident joins count as one point: their marks sit side by side in one place, a point kept on the X axis joined to one kept on the Y axis shows one At the origin mark, and Horizontal or Vertical between points joined to a line's ends marks that line. Several marks on one line or point sit side by side in screen pixels, in a fixed order, so they keep their size and spacing at every zoom. Dimensions keep their labels, and linear patterns and linked references keep their own controls, so they draw no mark. Marks lie beneath the sketch and its dimensions: where a mark covers a point, an edge, a dimension line or label, the origin, an axis, a profile grip or a profile edge, that geometry or dimension keeps the hover, click, double-click, right-click and drag. In Select, hovering a mark highlights the geometry its relation holds and the relation's other marks without rendering the sketch; hovering a relations or constraint issues row, or selecting geometry, highlights the marks of its relations. A click selects a mark's relation and replaces the geometry selection, Shift toggles and Escape clears; marks and canvas dimensions share one annotation selection and the status line names it, for example Parallel selected · Delete removes. Delete or Backspace removes the selected relations and dimensions in one undo step and keeps the geometry; a refused removal keeps the selection and shows its message. Double-click or Enter opens the relations list with the row active, and the right-click menu, the menu key and Shift+F10 offer Show in relations list and Delete on a relation mark, and Delete after the existing items on a dimension. Tab reaches the marks in Select, each named by its relation and operands, for example Parallel: Line 3 and Line 5; a mark that hides while focused returns focus to the canvas. With a drawing tool, during a pending Line chain or while a command picks geometry, marks take no pointer events or focus, and a drag keeps the pointer on what it moves. A sketch with more than 200 marks shows only the selected marks, those on selected or inspected geometry and those the pointer asks for: in Select, resting the pointer for about 120 ms on a point, an edge, a mark or a row in the relations or constraint issues list shows the marks of its relations, every new target starts the wait again, and the status line says how many marks the sketch has. A new Show relations display setting, on by default, hides every mark and drops a selected one when turned off; the relations list and the Constrain tools work as before. Show relations and On-part dimensions act independently: with dimensions hidden, marks still show, select, open their row and delete, a selected mark stays selected and a selected dimension leaves the selection, and with marks hidden, dimensions select as before. In the Dimension tool, marks take no pointer events or focus, also while it waits for its first pick, so its picks, preview and placement click reach the geometry and canvas beneath a mark.
warning: Potentially breaking for automation and people that drive the sketch canvas: relation marks are new focusable canvas buttons, so Tab in Select now stops on each mark, before the sketch's edges, points and dimension labels, and automation that counts focus stops or tabs to a point must allow for them. They take a click where nothing else lies, so a click on empty canvas beside a mark that used to clear the selection now selects that relation; points, edges, dimension lines and labels, the origin, axes and profile grips and edges beneath a mark keep their picks. Delete and Backspace now also remove selected relations: the canvas annotation selection, which held only dimensions, now holds relations and dimensions together, and cad_get_viewport.selectedSketchGeometrySet is empty while a relation mark is selected or the relations list was opened from one, as it already was for a selected dimension. Saved sketches keep their coordinate relations: a coordinate fixed at 0 draws the Coincident mark, both coordinates of one point, or of points that Coincident joins, at 0 draw one At the origin mark, whose status line and menu title read At the origin, and a coordinate fixed away from 0 or by a parameter, which 0.0.782 already draws and selects as a Distance dimension, draws no mark. A Coincident relation between two arc or circle centers is now named Concentric in the relations list, constraint issues and status line, where it read Coincident; automation that finds a relations row by its label must use the new name. The dimension right-click menu ends with a separator and Delete, which counts every selected relation and dimension when the menu acts on a larger selection. Potentially breaking for code that types its own icon component after a generated icon: the generated icons are now typed WorkbenchDrawnIconComponent, which requires paths, so a declaration such as const Custom: typeof PadIcon = forwardRef(...) no longer compiles; type such components WorkbenchIconComponent, which is unchanged. WebMCP tools, their arguments and results, the CAD schema, the solver and saved documents are unchanged. No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output.

checklist.schema: No CAD schema change: removals use the existing remove-sketch-relation edit through the same prepared batch as the relations list, and dimensions use the existing removal path. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol change; the Rust solver and committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. The new Show relations preference is a workbench display preference stored with the other CAD display settings, defaulting to on when absent, so older preference records load unchanged.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. The glyph layout is a pure function of the sketch graph, the view scale and the stacking order: operands come from cadSketchRelationPointIds and cadSketchRelationEntityIds through an exhaustive switch over relation kinds, offsets are screen pixels, and keys combine the relation ID, its kind and operands, so a reused ID never inherits a hover, selection or focus. Points are named by their Coincident identity through cadSketchPointIdentity, the per-graph resolver that dimension selection already caches, and every mark keeps the IDs of the relations it stands for. Names, stacking slots and keys come from the sketch graph as last edited, which a drag preview does not replace, so a drag only places the shown marks again; above the mark limit only the shown entries are placed. A placement reuses each mark that lands where it lay; during a drag the rows stay as they were, hidden where their mark moved, the moved marks draw as paths in a pointer-transparent group beside the layer, and only then does the layer ask for a compositor layer of its own (will-change: transform), so drag frames neither render nor repaint the rows. The glyph layer is memoized and receives neither the cursor, the cursor pick, the snap candidate nor the view signature, and each row takes primitive props and a stable action object, so drawing-cursor moves, a rectangle readout and a pending Line chain render no glyph row. Below the mark limit, hover lights operands and sibling marks through a highlight store that only the highlight overlay reads, so it renders no row and not the canvas; above the limit, in Select outside a drag, an applying edit or a pick, the layer also follows that store and the point or edge under the pointer, and shows the marks of the relations a target holds, judged on every point and edge each relation names, only once the pointer has rested on that target for 120 ms (CAD_SKETCH_RELATION_GLYPH_REVEAL_MS). Every change of target starts the wait again, and what the last target showed stays until the next one is shown; empty canvas keeps revealed marks for 400 ms so the pointer can cross to one. Leaving the canvas, a tool change, an edit or another sketch, Show relations off, a drag start and unmounting each clear the pending reveal, so no late timer shows marks for a stale target. Selected marks and the marks on selected or inspected geometry show at once. The layer is drawn before the dimension targets and the point and edge rows, so the browser hit test gives dimension lines, labels and geometry the pointer; dimensions pick only by their own elements, so that order decides every overlap with a dimension, and a mark press first asks the line cover and the 6 px geometry picker once per native event and declines without stopping propagation when either answers. Marks set pointer-events none and tabindex -1 unless the tool is Select with no pending path, pick or definition lock. A drag keeps the pointer captured by what it moves; during a drag or while an edit is applying, the layer takes no pointer events and the marks keep their tab stops, so starting or ending either renders no glyph row. Selections reuse the dimension annotation pick model, extended to every relation kind except linear patterns and linked references, and reconcile against the current graph after edits, undo and redo; CadSketchGraphSelection is unchanged. A removal of several relations and dimensions is one onEditMany batch and one undo step; a refused batch keeps the selection and shows its message. Merged with 0.0.782: a fixed-axis relation that isCadSketchDimensionRelation counts as a dimension, any value but a plain 0, draws no mark, and a plain-0 one draws the Coincident mark; X and Y at 0 on one Coincident identity draw one At the origin mark (isCadSketchOriginPair), and a mixed pair is not grouped. Canvas annotation picks are checked against cadSketchDrawnAnnotations, the drawn-dimension set of 0.0.782 plus whether marks are shown: a dimension picks only while the canvas draws it and a mark only while Show relations is on, so hiding dimensions drops a selected dimension and keeps a selected mark, hiding marks drops a selected mark and keeps a selected dimension, and an editor opened from a mark stays open while its mark is drawn. Marks sit beneath the dimension hit layer and the pointer-transparent overlay that draws the placement preview, and take no pointer events in any geometry pick, including the Dimension tool while it keeps placed dimensions interactive before its first pick. WebMCP tools and their arguments are unchanged; relation selection, like dimension selection, is not part of the agent viewport state, and docs/site/agents.md says that the selected geometry set is empty while a relation mark is selected.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. Sketch relations gain canvas marks with hover highlight, selection, Delete, double-click and Enter to open the relations list, a context menu and keyboard focus. The Constrain menu and the relations list show a relation icon. @wire-edm/icons-react gains 15 relation icons generated from scripts/icon-source.mjs, and every icon that createIcon makes now also carries its drawing as readonly paths, so the glyph layer draws many marks as a few paths; existing drawings and props are unchanged. WorkbenchIconComponent is unchanged: the generated icons are typed with the new exported WorkbenchDrawnIconComponent, which is WorkbenchIconComponent with readonly paths, so a component made outside createIcon and typed WorkbenchIconComponent still type-checks, and only code that reads paths needs the narrower type. A Show relations display preference is added.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved documents open unchanged and older releases open documents edited with this one; the new preference is ignored by older releases.
checklist.verification:
New tests:
- cadSketchRelationGlyphLayout.test.ts: placement for every relation kind, stacking order and spacing in screen pixels, coordinate marks, Concentric naming, relations that draw no mark, broken relations, and new mount keys for reused IDs. Points that Coincident joins: relations on either point stack in one place and keep their own IDs, X and Y at 0 on joined points draw one At the origin mark that names both relations, and Horizontal or Vertical between points joined to a line's ends marks that line. Point on curve marks its point and the curve. X at 0 and Y at 2 - 2 on one point draw one At the origin mark of the Coincident kind, Y at 0 alone draws On the X axis, a coordinate at 40 and one following a parameter that is 0 draw nothing, and a fixed point draws Fixed point. A placement keeps each mark a drag leaves in place as the same object.
- cadSketchRelationGlyphDrawing.test.ts: path data is read into absolute segments, placed by its centre at any size, and every relation icon fits its 10 px square.
- CadSketchCanvasRender.test.tsx: drawing-cursor moves, hover, a pending Line chain, and starting or ending a drag render no mark row, and below the limit hover does not render the mark layer. The mark layer lies beneath the dimension targets. During a drag the moved marks draw as paths beside the layer, their rows stay hidden in place, and the layer is composited apart only while the drag runs. Above the 200-mark limit, the selected marks and those on selected geometry are drawn at once, and those of a point, edge, mark or list row only once the pointer has rested on it for 120 ms, judged on every point and edge a relation names; the status line says so in Select only. With fake timers: nothing shows 1 ms before the rest and the marks show at it; each new target starts the wait again and the last marks stay until the next rest; leaving the canvas, a tool change and back, a sketch edit, Show relations off, a drag press and unmounting each clear the pending reveal timer, and none of them reveals marks later. Below the limit the layer does not render however long the pointer rests.
- CadWorkbench.test.tsx: selecting an edge lights every mark of its relations, select, Shift, Escape, Delete in one undo step, refused removal, double-click and Enter to the relations list, the context menu, list-row and selection highlighting, accessible names, no pointer events or focus with a drawing tool, a pending Line chain or a geometry pick, and the Show relations setting. Merged with 0.0.782: coordinates at 0, at 40 and following a parameter label the last two as Distances and mark only the first, and X and Y at 0 on Coincident-joined points draw one At the origin mark; Enter on an axis mark opens its On the X axis row, whose icon has the same paths as the Constrain menu's Coincident; Fix on a free point makes one fixed point with the Fixed mark; hiding on-part dimensions drops a selected dimension and keeps a selected mark, and each shows and selects without the other; in the Dimension tool the marks are inert while placed dimensions stay tab stops, a click on a mark selects nothing and Enter on one opens nothing.
- cadSketchDimensionSelection.test.ts names a Distance, On the Y axis, At the origin on one point and on joined points, and a coordinate at 0 with one away from it as 1 dimension and 1 relation. cadSketchDimensionSelection, CadSketchRelationsPanel and CadSettingsPanel tests were extended; the icon package test checks that each icon carries the path data it renders, and the packed-consumer type check confirms that a component made outside createIcon still satisfies WorkbenchIconComponent while WorkbenchDrawnIconComponent requires paths.
- e2e/cad-sketch-relation-glyphs.spec.ts in Chromium: hover, select, Delete and Undo, double-click to the list; during a drag the moved marks follow the edge beside the layer while their rows stay hidden in place, and after it the rows sit on the moved edge; a click beside a mark keeps the geometry pick; with Line, marks are inert while a chain is pending; a circle's diameter line crossing its fixed centre's mark keeps the hover, click, Delete, double-click and menu, and a size label over a mark keeps the click and the menu; the Dimension tool keeps its picks, preview hover and placement click over a mark, which is inert and absent from the hit test under the pointer, and the click places the distance.
- 25 mutations of the new rules each fail a test: layer order, Coincident identity in each comparison, hover followed below the limit and ignored above it, the related state on every operand, the curve mark, the line index, mark reuse, frozen and hidden rows, the composited layer and the moved-mark group; and for the rest delay, no delay, a wait not restarted on a new target, a list-row hover shown at once, and a pending reveal kept when the pointer leaves the canvas, through a sketch edit, in other tools and during a drag, after a drag press or by the effect cleanup. The cleanup mutation also fails each of the tool change, sketch edit, Show relations off, drag press and unmount checks on its own. After the merge with 0.0.782, 17 more mutations each fail a test: a coordinate at 0 drawn as Fix, a coordinate away from 0 keeping a mark, a parameter value counted as 0, X and Y at 0 not grouped, grouped by raw point ID or grouped with a Distance, the origin mark named after one axis, a fixed point drawn as Coincident, Fix adding two coordinate relations, the status line pairing a Distance with a coordinate at 0 or pairing by raw point ID, mark picks needing drawn dimensions, allowed while relations are hidden or needing the drawn dimension IDs, hidden dimensions picking while marks are shown, the editor kept open by drawn dimensions only, and marks interactive while Dimension waits for its first pick. Adding paths back to WorkbenchIconComponent makes icons:check fail on the packed consumer.

Checks:
- Full Vitest on the merged head: 559 files, 6567 tests passed.
- npm run build, npm run lint (zero findings), npm run ui:check, the e2e type-check and node scripts/check-release.mjs origin/main pass on the merged head; npm run icons:check passed before the merge, which does not touch the icon package.
- Chromium specs, run one at a time with two workers, all passed in round 1 (46 tests): cad-sketch-relation-glyphs, cad-sketch-constraints, cad-sketch-dimension-selection, cad-sketch-arc-trim, cad-sketch-editing, cad-sketch-context-editing, cad-sketch-selectable-axes, cad-sketch-reference-dimensions, cad-sketch-line-chain, cad-sketch-point-on-line, cad-sketch-profile-copy and cad-sketch-circle-trim. On the merged head, each run alone with two workers: cad-sketch-relation-glyphs (5 tests), cad-sketch-axis-dimension (1), cad-sketch-dimension-placement (1), cad-sketch-dimension-selection (4), cad-sketch-dimension-points (1), cad-sketch-constraints (28) and cad-sketch-selectable-axes (1), 41 tests, all passed.

Measurements:
- Setup: Chromium at 4x CPU slowdown, branch and main production builds run alternately, medians of 8 runs against main 0.0.781 before the merge. The sketch is a grid of 10 mm rectangles with Horizontal and Vertical on every edge; the drag is 60 moves of one corner and hover is 150 moves across the canvas.
- 200 marks shown: a drag took 4.7 s against 4.8 s, with long tasks 0.6 s against 1.0 s and handled P50 55 ms against 60 ms. Hover handled P50 was 24.1 ms against 25.2 ms in Select and 23.6 ms against 23.2 ms with Rectangle. A second build of the same code read 8% more drag time and the same long-task time.
- 400 marks shown, with the limit raised for the measurement only: the drag took 25% longer than main, with 26% more long-task time.
- 400 relations above the limit, none shown until the pointer asks: without a rest delay the drag took 4% longer, and Select hover handled P50 was 3.4 ms above main, the cost of showing the marks of each hovered edge.
- Rest delay, a session alternating main, the code without the delay and two delay variants, medians of 8: Select hover handled P50 above the limit read +2.8 ms without the delay, +1.5 ms when a new target hides the last marks at once and +1.2 ms when they stay until the next rest, with long-task time +97%, +48% and -1%, and a drag above the limit +6%, +3% and +0% in time. Those runs split into slower first and faster second runs of each build, and the median of 8 falls between them; the second runs alone read +2.7, -0.7 and +0.3 ms. Keeping the last marks until the next rest measured cheaper and was kept.
- Final build against main, medians of 12: Select hover handled P50 above the limit 26.4 ms against 26.9 ms (-0.6 ms), with no long tasks in either; at 200 marks below the limit, Select hover 23.9 ms against 25.1 ms and a drag 3% longer with 13% less long-task time.
- After the merge with 0.0.783, a session alternated main 0.0.783, the branch and an overlay prototype, 6 rounds, medians of 12. Above the limit, with 240 relations, the branch is even with main: a drag +2% in time and long tasks, hover +3% in time and handled P50 within 0.1 ms. At 200 marks a drag took 7% longer with 2% more long-task time, and hover took 15% longer in Select and 17% with Rectangle, with handled P50 about 1 ms and P95 about 17 ms above main. Earlier sessions read 200-mark hover as even.
- A trace puts the hover cost in paint and layerize work. Hover changes almost nothing in the canvas, yet each move repaints and re-layerizes its layer, and the marks add their paint chunks to every pass; giving the caption, the canvas or the mark layer a compositor layer of its own did not close the gap. With Rectangle, Paint took 285 ms against 195 ms with the marks hidden and 157 ms on main, and Layerize 240 to 330 ms against 185 ms and 130 to 170 ms. The mark layer renders nothing on these moves.
- The cost is not from the merge. A session alternated main 0.0.781, the pre-merge head, main 0.0.783 and the merged head. Against its own main, the pre-merge head read +26% hover time in Select and +38% with Rectangle, and the merged head +24% and +18%. A drag at 200 marks read -4% and -5% in time. At 100 marks, hover took 11 to 17% longer than main, and a drag 4 to 33% longer depending on the session.
- The moved marks and the hover ring stay in the canvas. A prototype that portalled them into the pointer overlay measured drag long tasks at -14% against main, where the branch read +2%, but handled P50 at +9.5 ms against +7.2 ms. That is inside the 10-point spread between two builds running the same code above the limit, and its hover matched the branch's. The overlay would also draw them over the geometry and dimensions.
- The limit of 200 is kept: a lower one would not remove the hover cost, which shows at 100 marks too.

Out of scope: no controller or machine verification applies, because output is unchanged.

publicNotes.summary: Sketch relations show as marks on the canvas that you can select and delete.
changes: Each sketch relation draws a small mark on the canvas beside the geometry it holds, with the same symbol the Constrain menu and the relations list now show.
Hover a mark to highlight the geometry its relation holds; hovering a relations or issue row, or selecting geometry, highlights the marks of its relations.
Click a mark to select its relation, Shift-click to add or remove one and Escape to clear. Delete or Backspace removes the selected relations and dimensions in one undo step.
Double-click a mark, or press Enter on it, to open the relations list on its row. Right-click it for Show in relations list and Delete.

A point that Fix holds shows a Fixed mark, a point kept on an axis shows a Coincident mark, and a point at the origin through both coordinates shows one At the origin mark. A coordinate fixed away from 0 is a Distance dimension and draws no mark. Points that Coincident joins share one place for their marks, and a Coincident relation between two centers reads Concentric.
Marks never take a click from the geometry or the dimension lines and labels under them, and they ignore the pointer while you draw, during a Line chain or while a command picks geometry.
In a sketch with more than 200 marks, rest the pointer for a moment on a point, an edge or a relations row to show the marks of its relations.

Settings → CAD → Display → Show relations hides the marks; the relations list and the Constrain tools keep working. It works independently of On-part dimensions, so marks stay selectable with dimensions hidden.
publicNotes.compatibility: Sketches keep using existing relation kinds, so earlier releases open them. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: Tab in the sketch now stops on relation marks, and a click on a mark beside the geometry selects that relation; turn off Settings → CAD → Display → Show relations to hide them. Automation that finds a relations row named Coincident between two centers should use Concentric.
